findings.title: `.small-action` becomes a flex container but its children still rely on floats
findings.body: `.small-action` now gets `display: flex` (line 264), but `.topic-avatar` keeps `float: left`, `.small-action-desc .avatar` keeps `float: left`, and `button` keeps `float: right` (line 309). Floats have no effect on flex items, so the action button that was previously pushed to the right edge of the row will now sit directly after the description text, and the `clear: both` on the container is dead. To keep the previous visual result the button needs `margin-left: auto` (or the description needs `flex: 1`), and the float declarations should be removed since they are now misleading. As written this is a visible layout regression in every small-action row in topics.

findings.title: Float fallbacks removed; header layout has no fallback in browsers without flexbox
findings.body: The `.title { float: left }` and `.panel { float: right }` rules were deleted and replaced solely with flexbox (`@include flexbox()` on `.contents`, `margin-left: auto` + `order(3)` on `.panel`). In any browser that supports none of the prefixed/unprefixed flex display values (e.g. IE9, older Android stock browsers), the title and panel will now stack as block elements with the panel below the logo, instead of degrading to the old floated layout. If those browsers are still in the support matrix, keep the float declarations as a fallback (they are harmlessly ignored inside a flex container).

findings.title: `-ms-align-items` is not a real property
findings.body: The `align-items` mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment`. No version of IE/Edge ever implemented a `-ms-align-items` property (IE10 uses `-ms-flex-align`, which is already emitted on the previous line; IE11+ uses unprefixed `align-items`). This line is dead output added to every use of the mixin and should be removed. Note also that `-webkit-box-align` / `-ms-flex-align` use different keyword names (`start`/`end`) than the standard `flex-start`/`flex-end`, so the mixin silently produces invalid legacy values if called with those; it currently only works because callers pass `center` and `baseline`.

findings.title: PR title/description do not describe the change
findings.body: The PR is titled "Optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins" and its description is just "Test 5", but the diff is a layout/visual refactor (floats → flexbox, padding/margin changes in `.small-action` and `.extra-info-wrapper`) with no performance-related change. The title is misleading and the description gives reviewers nothing to verify against (e.g. which screenshots/pages were checked). The description should state the intended visual outcome and what was tested.
